question: to the Commission Arash Saeidi (The Left) Subject:

On 29 April 2026, Eurostat published a report on the performance of the agricultural sector, which stated that, in the EU, the sector comprises 7.4 million full-time equivalent workers. Of those, non-salaried workers – farm managers and their families – amount to 5 million. Behind the figures lie realities. Family workers are primarily women, the farm managers’ wives. Their work is often unsalaried, which means they have no social rights, including those relating to unemployment and pensions. Salaried labour, on the other hand, is largely provided by seasonal workers who, by definition, face a very high level of job insecurity. In light of this: 1.
Does the Commission intend to impose social clauses in quality labels and contractual conditions?
Does the Commission intend to create an intermittent agricultural worker status enabling such workers to continue to receive wages out of season?
Does the Commission intend to take steps to ensure that non-salaried labour performed by farm managers’ families is recognised?
